newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Sarkozy supports bolder income tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: France's Sarkozy supports bolder income tax cuts.

text.p: Former budget minister Nicolas Sarkozy called in a newspaper interview for further income tax cuts and interest rate reductions.
"I think that for the next two or three years we can and we must go further that the cuts of 75 billion francs already targeted," Sarkozy told French daily La Tribune Desfosses.
The government plans to cut income taxes by 75 billion francs over the next five years, including cuts of 25 billion francs on income earned in 1996 and payable in 1997.
Sarkozy, a Conservative deputy in the National Assembly close to former Prime Minister Edouard Balladur, also called for further easing in France's monetary policy.
